citation.title: RELEASE: Fossil fuel lobbyists eclipse delegations from most climate vulnerable nations at COP29 climate talks
citation.venue_or_publisher: Kick Big Polluters Out (campaign coalition website)
citation.type: press release (web page) with short methodology note; NGO campaign material

question: How many fossil fuel lobbyists were granted access to COP29 (Baku), how this compares with country delegations, and how many came via trade associations or inside Party delegations.
data: UNFCCC provisional list of participants for COP29, published 11 November 2024; matched against KBPO lists from COP26, COP27, COP28 and external lobbyist registers. Release dated 15 November 2024; over 52,000 participants in total.
method: List downloaded, cleaned and deduplicated with automated tools and manual processing; organisations matched against earlier KBPO lists and external registers; for COP29 a web search for each organisation and delegation was fed to a Large Language Model (retrieval-augmented generation) that judged whether it was a fossil fuel lobbyist and gave an explanation and references; all results then manually fact-checked and cross-checked with earlier years. Anonymised list available on request (not published here).

definitions.definition: Any individual delegate who represents an organisation, or is a member of a delegation, that can reasonably be assumed to aim to influence policy or legislation in the interests of the fossil fuel industry or a particular fossil fuel company and its shareholders. Applies to delegations as well as organisations.
definitions.quote: we consider a fossil fuel lobbyist any individual delegate that represents an organisation or is a member of a delegation that can be reasonably assumed to have the objective of influencing
definitions.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Methodology, para 31)

definitions.definition: Counted only if reasonable assumption of intent to influence policy in the interests of a fossil fuel corporation and its shareholders. Other industries (finance, agribusiness, transport) are noted as present but excluded.
definitions.quote: Other polluting industries deeply implicated in the climate crisis such as finance, agribusiness, and transportation are also present, although they are not included in this analysis.
definitions.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 12)

definitions.definition: Registrants declare their delegation, which can be an official country delegation (or party overflow), a UN body, an intergovernmental organisation, an NGO or a media institution. Badge types are not otherwise defined.
definitions.quote: an official country delegation (or party overflow), a UN body, an intergovernmental organisation, a non-government organisation, or a media institution
definitions.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Methodology, para 28)

definitions.definition: Not defined. The release refers to calls for clear conflict of interest policies and accountability measures.
definitions.quote: establishing clear conflict of interest policies and accountability measures
definitions.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 13)

proxies.indicator: The organisation the participant declared at registration, and the delegation they are part of (organisation affiliation, role and relationship to organisation are mandatory fields from COP28).
proxies.quote: must declare the organisation they work for, the nature of their relationship to this organisation, their role, and the delegation they’re part of
proxies.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Methodology, para 28)

proxies.concept: fossil fuel link of an organisation or delegation
proxies.indicator: Identifiable connections found by programmatic web search: company websites, social media profiles, news articles, other public information; judged by an LLM and fact-checked by people.
proxies.quote: looked for identifiable connections to the fossil fuel industry. These sources usually consist of company websites, their social media profiles, news articles, and other publicly available information.
proxies.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Methodology, para 33)

proxies.indicator: Match against KBPO lists from COP26, COP27, COP28 and external lobbyist registers.
proxies.quote: matched the organisations at this year's COP against lists of fossil fuel lobbyists we have identified at COP26, COP27 and COP28, as well as external registers of lobbyists.
proxies.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Methodology, para 30)

proxies.concept: trade association with fossil fuel representation
proxies.indicator: Listed as top ten 'trade associations ... representing the fossil fuel industry' with delegate counts; the list includes cross-sector business bodies, a development fund and a research centre, so the label is broad.
proxies.quote: The top ten biggest trade associations in attendance representing the fossil fuel industry are the International Emissions Trading Association (43 delegates)
proxies.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Notes to the editor, para 25)

findings.claim: At least 1773 fossil fuel lobbyists registered for COP29.
findings.quote: At least 1773 fossil fuel lobbyists have been granted access to the COP29 summit in Baku
findings.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 1)

findings.claim: Only three country delegations were larger than the lobbyist total: Azerbaijan 2229, Brazil 1914, Türkiye 1862.
findings.quote: only outnumbered by delegations sent by host Azerbaijan (2229), COP30 host Brazil (1914), and Türkiye (1862)
findings.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 2)

findings.claim: Lobbyists outnumbered all delegates of the ten most climate vulnerable nations combined (1033).
findings.quote: more passes to COP29 than all the delegates from the 10 most climate vulnerable nations combined (1033)
findings.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 4)

findings.claim: Fossil-linked people sat inside national delegations: examples named for Japan (Sumitomo), Canada (Suncor, Tourmaline), UK (20 lobbyists), Italy (Eni, Enel). No total for fossil-linked delegates inside Party delegations is given.
findings.quote: Japan brought coal giant Sumitomo as part of its delegation; Canada bought oil producers Suncor and Tourmaline; the United Kingdom brought 20 lobbyists
findings.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 6)

findings.claim: Many lobbyists came through trade associations; eight of the top ten groups were from the Global North; the largest, IETA, brought 43 people including TotalEnergies and Glencore representatives.
findings.quote: Eight of the top 10 trade groups with the most lobbyists came from the Global North.
findings.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 5)

findings.claim: Time series reported by KBPO: 636 at COP27, more than 2,450 at COP28, 1773 at COP29; total participants fell from over 84,000 to over 52,000.
findings.quote: more than 2,450 fossil fuel lobbyists were granted access to the COP28 climate talks in Dubai, up from 636 the year before that in Egypt.
findings.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 15)

findings.claim: Mandatory declaration of who participants represent began at COP28, which the authors say reveals people who would earlier have attended undeclared (so comparisons across years are affected).
findings.quote: COP28 was the first time COP attendees were required to disclose who they represent, revealing many lobbyists who would likely have attended previous COPs incognito.
findings.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 14)

limitations.point: Advocacy press release, not a peer-reviewed study; no author names; methodology is five short paragraphs with no codebook, no classification examples and no accuracy or error rate for the LLM step.
The authors state that other sectors (finance, agribusiness, transport) are excluded, so business presence overall is not counted; no sector breakdown of business delegates is given.
limitations.quote: they are not included in this analysis
limitations.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 12)

limitations.point: Counts are of whole delegations/organisations judged to be fossil-linked, so every member of a flagged delegation counts as a lobbyist; the inference rests on 'reasonably assumed' intent. The release does not separate Party badge, overflow badge and observer holders in its totals.
limitations.quote: can be reasonably assumed to have the objective of influencing
limitations.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (para 31)

limitations.point: Count is 'at least' and comes from the provisional list published 11 November 2024, before the final list; the count of 1773 and the per-country delegation sizes may differ from the final list.
limitations.quote: The UNFCCC published a provisional list of the participants on 11th November 2024.
limitations.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Methodology, para 29)

limitations.point: The list of top trade associations mixes bodies with different roles (e.g. a chamber of commerce, OPEC Fund, a research centre) under one label, and how each was judged fossil-linked is not shown.

Underlying list of lobbyists is not public, only anonymised on request; results cannot be reproduced from the page. Page also carries advocacy and political statements (Palestine, US politics) that are outside the counting method.
limitations.quote: An anonymised list of the 1773 fossil fuel lobbyists is available on request
limitations.page: Industry influx escalates call to protect talks from Big Polluters (Methodology, para 27)
